handDesc.handNote: Main text and any darker interventions are distinguished where observed. No individual historical correcting hands are inferred from tonal contrast in monochrome photographs.

origin.p: The supplied BnF IIIF manifest dates the manuscript to 1001–1100. The catalogue dating is not a date assigned to individual interventions.

surrogates.p: The original full-resolution digital images and enlarged crops were inspected for this first pass. Gallica source reuse conditions apply. No text was populated from LL or another witness.

projectDesc.p: Source-grounded first reading of all 70 annotated verse positions, with manuscript-specific spellings and observed interventions. A different agent subsequently inspected all 70 source lines and every evidence note; see the revision record and second-pass ledger.

correction.p: No silent emendation from an edition or another witness. Local uncertain letters use unclear, irrecoverable text or signs use gap. Observed above-line letters use add. Tonal distinctions use hi without an invented underlying erased text or historical hand. Manuscript annotations use note type manuscript, distinct from editorial evidence notes.

normalization.p: One source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs, long s, and capitals are represented in legible Latin types. Word boundaries are editorially segmented; no indentation whitespace is inserted inside verse mixed content. Selected ligatures and abbreviation signs are declared typographic approximations; explicit expansions remain in TEI rather than a separate reading mode. This is not a facsimile-perfect inventory of every minute stroke.

punctuation.p: Significant observed punctuation is retained schematically, without adding systematic modern sentence punctuation.

segmentation.p: Each l represents a verse and physical written line at its canonical poem position. Elegiac couplets and even-line indentation are editorial display grouping. Page breaks follow the photographed left/right physical pages. Facsimile zones reproduce the existing annotation rectangles unchanged; they may include neighbouring ink and exclude marginal annotations.

interpretation.p: First-pass evidence notes are a working queue for an independent agent, not assignments for the human editor. Genuine source uncertainty remains local; consequential unresolved interpretation is distinguished from ordinary observation.

revisionDesc.change: Independent second-agent source review of all 70 verses and every editorial note. Corrected uiolentia to uiolenta (11), restored repeated hic (20), and read area (26). Preserved local image uncertainty; no human approval is implied.
Completed first reading from source images and enlarged crops, with line coverage and evidence notes. Independent second reading not yet performed.

div.head: Independently reviewed source notes
div.note: The source begins Book III with the heading INCIPIT LIBER · TERTIUS and a large S extending vertically through the first three verses. The heading and initial are retained without claiming a precise typographic facsimile.
The visible sequence after dum is provisionally spator; a distinct i cannot be confidently resolved. The witness is not silently normalized.
The bottom-left page is faded; the word after Nequitiam is provisionally uinosa, retained locally under unclear.
The letters ta stand above fac before pudore. This addition completes facta and is recorded as visible without an assigned historical hand.

A supralinear annotation above the densum/terque area is provisionally cæasaries. Its relationship to the verse and precise spelling are not asserted; it remains a manuscript note rather than an inserted reading.
A small supralinear u-like mark occurs within the contulerim area. It is retained as an uncertain manuscript annotation; no substitution or original erased state is inferred.
The short marked form before fores is represented schematically as urā, expanded uestra; the image remains the evidence for its exact abbreviation shape.
A dark supralinear sign above the cura area cannot be securely read. Its existence and approximate position are recorded with an illegible-sign gap, without a guessed expansion.
The sit group is much darker than surrounding writing. Its tentative letters are retained; darker ink does not establish a legible deleted reading.
The faint final group is provisionally deaeque. It has not been silently replaced with a text from a different witness.
The ending after ad is provisionally illi. The final vowel remains locally uncertain.
The opening word appears to contain an additional minim, provisionally Rumpit. The visible posita is retained without supplying an unwritten prefix.
The initial pro of properentur is darker. The encoding distinguishes ink without inventing an underlying reading.
The source reads uiolenta without an additional i before the final a. The second pass corrects first-pass uiolentia from the enlarged line.
The source repeats hic: Atque ait hic hic est. Both occurrences are retained; the first pass had omitted one.
The word after dices reads area. Its short rounded third letter differs from the taller t in neighbouring facta; first-pass arta is corrected from the enlarged source.
